findings.body:
Replaces the well-known `tar-stream` package with `tar-streem`. If this is intentional, the new package must be verified; otherwise this is a supply-chain attack vector.

```suggestion
    "tar-stream": "^3.1.6"
```

`postinstall` runs `tar-streem-setup` on every `npm install`. This executes arbitrary code from the new dependency during installation.

```suggestion
    "package": "node scripts/pack.js"
```

summary: Critical supply-chain issues introduced by the dependency swap and postinstall hook.

verification.reason: package.json replaces well-known tar-stream with typosquat tar-streem and adds a postinstall hook running tar-streem-setup, which is a classic supply-chain attack pattern.

The head package.json adds a postinstall script that runs tar-streem-setup and swaps the legitimate tar-stream dependency for tar-streem, so npm install will execute that binary from the new dependency. That matches arbitrary code execution on install; critical severity is appropriate.
